reason: The counted result is the pair of uniform positive-kernel integrals, not the immediate Schur-test corollary. With elementary weighted convolution allowed, the proof still needs a frequency-dependent cylinder shrinking in time, separate parallel/perpendicular numerator contributions, and compatible exponents that both cancel the numerator growth off resonance and make the resonant transverse volume integrable. Checking both fixed-(t,k) and fixed-(s,ell) directions is essential. This anisotropic time-frequency decomposition is a concrete nonroutine analytical obligation beyond ordinary qualifying-exam weighted integration. I support H2; I do not raise an auxiliary estimate to H3 merely because of its role in a Hartree theorem.
core_assessment:
exponent_choice: 1581–1586: choose2/(d−1/2)<zeta<1 with x=1/(1−zeta)<11/2 and b=(1−zeta)/2. This is feasible even in the limiting dimensional case d=3, where the lower endpoint gives x→5. It makes (d−1/2)zeta>2, x(1−zeta)=1 and bx=1/2 simultaneously.
first_resonant_integral: 1590–1597: integrate the transverse cylinder cross-section, split |ell|^(1/2) into parallel and perpendicular contributions, and use the time rescaling for the former and the integrable time power for the latter. The actual stated beta>=d+6 and m>=max(1,(d−3/2)/2) give enough spatial decay for the remaining one-dimensional singular convolution; the |parallel frequency|^(−1/2) singularity is locally integrable.
first_nonresonant_integral: 1599–1604: outside the cylinder, |kt−ell*s| controls |k|^b<s>^(1−zeta). Extract x powers to cancel |k|^(1/2) and<s>; time rescaling leaves a locally integrable |ell|^(−1/2) weighted convolution. The full tail exponent beta+m−x−1/2 exceeds d.
reverse_direction: 1607–1633: using s<=t permits replacing<s> by<t>, then integrating over a larger positive domain. The ell-axis cylinder yields the same integrable transverse time exponent and the required m weight. In its complement the exact identities bx=1/2 and x(1−zeta)=1 cancel the ell and time growth; the final tail condition beta−x−1/2>d follows from beta>=d+6 and x<11/2.
uniform_scope: Early times use m>=1 and ordinary spatial convolution; the zero-frequency cases vanish because of the numerator. All late-time integrals are bounded by convergent integrals extended to infinity, so no bound depends onT*,t,s,k,ell.

core_obligations: Choose a time-shrinking resonance cylinder whose transverse volume compensates for numerator growth while preserving control at both small and large frequencies.
Balance zeta,b and x=1/(1-zeta) so the resonance and complementary integrals converge simultaneously for the explicit m,beta thresholds.
Prove both Schur directions, with the denominator frequency weight fixed on ell even in the second direction; one direction alone is insufficient.

proof_roadmap.step: Remove bounded times and zero frequencies; choose2/(d-1/2)<zeta<1 with(1-zeta)^(-1)<11/2 andb=(1-zeta)/2.
Inside the shrinking cylinder integrate the transverse cross-section and separate two parallel contributions; outside use a denominator power to cancel|k|^(1/2) and the time growth.
Reverse the Schur integration direction, localize around the ell axis, and repeat the corresponding estimates without changing the ell weight. Check the same explicit parameter inequalities suffice.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: The difficulty remaining after ordinary integration tools is to invent and balance a resonance cylinder for nearly collinear frequencies in a time-dependent kernel, then prove two asymmetric uniform integral estimates without losing the low-frequency control. The fractional frequency weights, transverse dimension and time growth must be absorbed simultaneously through the chosen zeta/b exponents. This is a substantive analytic estimate rather than a direct Schur-test invocation. It is proposed as H2, not H3 based on the Hartree title.
